paras: The shooting of Willis Reed took place at Columbus, Texas, on a Saturday night in late November 1880, probably 20 November, when officers trying to arrest Reed, a Black man, shot him three times. Reed was captured and handed to a doctor, who expected him to recover; the only known report is a short item in the Brenham Weekly Banner.

According to the Banner, Reed "resisted arrest and tried to shoot the officers" at Columbus on "last Saturday night week." The item did not say why the officers sought to arrest him, name the officers, or give the place in town where the shooting occurred. After the officers put three bullets in his body, Reed was captured and "turned over to a doctor for repairs."
The doctor, the Banner reported, thought he would cure Reed. No later report of Reed's recovery or death, of charges against him, or of any inquiry into the shooting appears in the coverage.

The shooting ran on 2 December 1880 as one paragraph in the Banner's front-page roundup of Texas news, between an infanticide arrest in Gonzales County and the sugar crop in Fort Bend County. The brief identified Reed only as "a negro," gave no source, and presented the claim that he had tried to shoot the officers as fact. Its tone was light, describing medical care for three gunshot wounds as "repairs."
No other paper's version of the shooting has been found, and the Black press of 1880 is not represented in the coverage.
